solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Silly sitcom about North American monk (8)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a noun used attributively; MONASTIC is the adjective, as in 'monk life'.

indicators.note: silly letters are foolish, so rearranged
the jumbled SITCOM goes about, around, NA

annotation.surface: A critic sneers at a daft TV comedy about a monk from America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Silly sitcom' reads as a review, but 'Silly' only tells you to shuffle the letters of 'sitcom'.
annotation.definitionFit: Monastic means relating to monks, as in the monk life.

entries.clue: Principal part of foot (4)

blocks.note: chief, the sense of the prefix in words like 'archbishop'
the raised curve on the underside of the foot

annotation.surface: An anatomy lesson on the main section of the foot.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase, 'the main part of the foot', but splits into two separate meanings.
annotation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means chief, and the arch is part of the foot.

entries.clue: Taunts start to trouble moderates (6)

indicators.note: the start of 'trouble' is its first letter

annotation.surface: Heckling begins to rattle the political moderates.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moderates' looks like a noun for centrist politicians; it is the verb, meaning lessens.
annotation.definitionFit: To taunt someone is to tease them.

entries.clue: Obsessive about one’s pet? (6)

indicators.note: ANAL goes about, around, IM

blocks.note: anal = fussily obsessive, short for anal-retentive

annotation.surface: A fussy owner fixated on their pet.
annotation.walkthrough: "One's" reads as a possessive, but it is the contraction of 'one is', giving I'M.
annotation.definitionFit: A pet is an animal; the question mark flags that a pet is only one kind.

entries.clue: Vehicle owner crashed, showing signs of stress (8)

indicators.note: crashed letters are wrecked into a new order

annotation.surface: A driver who has just crashed their car looks shaken.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crashed' fits a car so well that it hides its job: it tells you to shuffle 'owner'.
annotation.definitionFit: Careworn describes a face marked by worry and strain.

entries.clue: Hint of culture every so often (4)

indicators.note: take a letter every so often, here every other one

annotation.surface: An occasional trace of refinement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Hint of culture' reads as one phrase, a touch of sophistication; 'of' is just the link.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a hint or a clue is a small piece of information that points you toward an answer.

entries.clue: Tenure of corrupt cardinal (8)

indicators.note: corrupted letters are twisted out of shape

annotation.surface: The term in office of a crooked Catholic cardinal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' points to a churchman; here it is a cardinal number, one used for counting.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: cardinal numbers are the counting numbers (one, two, three), as opposed to ordinals like first and second.

entries.clue: Completely unknown supporter (4)

blocks.note: all = completely, as in all alone
algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

annotation.surface: A backer nobody has ever heard of.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Completely unknown' reads as one phrase; it splits into ALL and a mathematical unknown.
annotation.definitionFit: An ally is someone who supports you.

entries.clue: Ways to bear love and poignancy (6)

indicators.note: PATHS bear, carry, the O inside them

blocks.note: love = nil = O, as in tennis

annotation.surface: Methods for enduring love and heartbreak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bear love' suggests enduring heartache; 'bear' only means carry inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that stirs pity or sadness: poignancy.

entries.clue: Disheartened, many watch rubbish (2,3)

indicators.note: losing its heart, its middle letters

annotation.surface: Feeling low, lots of people sit watching trash TV.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Watch rubbish' reads as viewing junk television; 'my eye!' is a dated exclamation meaning nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: 'My eye!' is an exclamation of disbelief, like 'rubbish!'

entries.clue: Some apparently backward times (3)

indicators.note: only some of the letters of 'apparently' are used
those letters read backward

blocks.note: the 4th to 6th letters, a present-tense verb, read right to left

annotation.surface: Some periods seem behind the times.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Apparently' looks like an adverb for the surface; it is just the word that holds the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: An era is a period of time, as in 'those were the times'.

entries.clue: Former secret police’s inactivity (6)

blocks.note: the Stasi were East Germany's secret police

annotation.surface: The idleness of a disbanded secret police force.
annotation.walkthrough: The Stasi were the state security service of East Germany until 1990.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from the Greek for standing, it names a condition where nothing moves or changes.

entries.clue: Son tears blanket (8)

blocks.note: s = son, as in family trees

annotation.surface: A child cries into his security blanket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tears' could be rips, and 'blanket' a bed covering; here blanket is the adjective, as in a blanket ban.
annotation.definitionFit: A blanket rule is sweeping: it covers everything.

entries.clue: Sponge pudding making comeback, I see (6)

indicators.note: the word comes back, reading right to left

blocks.note: a fool is a pudding of fruit folded into cream

annotation.surface: A sponge pudding is back on the menu, I notice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sponge pudding' reads as one dessert, but 'Sponge' stands alone as the definition. A fool is a British dessert of fruit and cream.
annotation.definitionFit: A loofah is the dried fibrous gourd used as a bath sponge.

entries.clue: In a state about radioactive substance (8)

indicators.note: STATE goes about, around, IN

annotation.surface: Someone flustered by a dangerous radioactive material.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as the idiom for flustered, so the eye takes it as one phrase; the three words are used literally and separately.
annotation.definitionFit: Astatine is a rare radioactive element, number 85.

entries.clue: Second finest horror film (6)

blocks.note: s = second, the unit of time
the cream = the best, the pick

annotation.surface: Ranking the runner-up in the best horror movies.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Second finest' reads as a ranking; it splits into S and CREAM. Scream is the 1996 slasher film.
annotation.definitionFit: Scream is a well-known horror film series.

entries.clue: Deadly cannon finally changing hands (6)

indicators.note: the final letter swaps one hand for the other: R (right) becomes L (left)

blocks.note: a mortar is a short cannon

annotation.surface: A lethal gun that ends up with a new owner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Changing hands' suggests a sale; it means swapping right for left, R for L.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a mortal blow or mortal danger is one that causes or threatens death.

entries.clue: Stay in, worried for soundness of mind (6)

indicators.note: worried letters are shaken about

annotation.surface: Advice to stay home when anxious, to protect your mental health.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is lockdown advice, and 'worried' fits it as a feeling rather than an instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A dictionary gloss: the word comes from Latin sanus, healthy, so it is literally a healthy mind.

entries.clue: Part of God’s acre dutifully hallowed (6)

indicators.note: the answer is part of the following letters

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of God's through acre into the start of dutifully

annotation.surface: A corner of a churchyard, dutifully kept holy.
annotation.walkthrough: God's acre is an old name for a churchyard, which makes the picture of holy ground fit the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to hallow is to make holy, so anything hallowed has been set apart as holy.

entries.clue: Eggs on vacuous airheads at first (3)

indicators.note: take each word's first letter

annotation.surface: Urging on empty-headed fools.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Eggs on' reads as the verb for urging someone forward; 'Eggs' is the plural noun.
annotation.definitionFit: Ova are egg cells, the plural of ovum.

entries.clue: Quietly copy conclusion of her essay (5)

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

annotation.surface: A student secretly plagiarises the ending of a classmate's essay.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is cheating in class; each word is doing a small job instead.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from academic life: a student writes a term paper, and a scholar presents a paper at a conference.

entries.clue: Caught top spy (4)

indicators.note: to catch a remark is to hear it, so what follows is a sound, not a spelling

blocks.note: the summit of a mountain, spoken and then spelt as a different word

annotation.surface: A leading spy has been captured.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like an arrest; it means heard. 'Spy' is the verb, to glimpse.
annotation.definitionFit: To peek is to take a quick look, to spy.

entries.clue: Forthcoming time on board yacht at sea (6)

indicators.note: a passenger on board a boat is inside it, so the letter goes inside the boat word
letters at sea are all over the place

annotation.surface: Upcoming leisure hours sailing on a yacht.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Forthcoming' suggests upcoming, fitting the holiday picture; it means talkative.
annotation.definitionFit: A forthcoming person is open and talkative: chatty.

entries.clue: Culmination of cases of academic malpractice (4)

indicators.note: the outer letters encase each word

blocks.note: first and last letters of academic

annotation.surface: The worst of a string of university cheating scandals.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cases' suggests disciplinary cases; it means the outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from the Greek for a point or peak, it names the highest point something reaches.

entries.clue: Quaker colonist, regularly pregnant (4)

indicators.note: take letters at regular intervals

annotation.surface: A settler's wife who is often expecting.
annotation.walkthrough: William Penn was the Quaker who founded Pennsylvania.
annotation.definitionFit: William Penn was a Quaker and colonist who founded Pennsylvania.

entries.clue: Inciting bent mate to go astray (8)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Inciting' is a gerund here, a noun like ABETMENT.

indicators.note: letters that go astray wander out of order

annotation.surface: Urging a crooked friend to go off the rails.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bent' is British slang for crooked, which suits the crime picture, but here it is fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Abetment is the act of inciting or encouraging a crime.
